# Brownfield Opportunities — US contaminated-site atlas for data-center & power-generation siting

> An open dataset and interactive map of ~46,800 federally-tracked contaminated and formerly-used US sites (EPA Superfund/NPL, EPA ACRES brownfields, DOD FUDS, DOD BRAC), enriched with grid, gas, flood, opportunity-zone, climate, and tax-incentive data, and scored 0–100 for four siting use cases: hosting a data-center electrical LOAD, building new power GENERATION, siting a MANUFACTURING plant, and siting a 1–20 MWe MICROREACTOR.

The dashboard is a static, dependency-light site (Leaflet + vanilla JS — no backend, no build step). Every data file is open JSON under `data/`. Rankings come from `screens.js`: each use (data center, solar farm, port industry, nickel refinery, large reactor, SMR, microreactor, civilian nuclear site, coal plant, retired heavy industry) is 2-5 pass/fail checks with a cited threshold, tagged as an agency number or ours. Rank = checks met, then fewest unknowns, then one stated tie-breaker; missing data never passes. `node scripts/screen.js explain <id>` reproduces any rank from the shell.

## Site

- [Interactive dashboard](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/): Screens (ranked shortlists with the method on top), Map, Table, Retired industry, Coal plants, Nuclear, DOE Sites, Data & methods; per-site panel opens with each screen's checks.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/pranava0x0/brownfield-opportunities): connectors, schema, tests, and refresh tooling.

## Data files (open JSON, served from data/)

- [sites.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/sites.json): Superfund/NPL sites, the eager first-paint set (~1,900 records). Mirror of superfund-npl.json.
- [epa-acres.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/epa-acres.json): ~36,000 EPA ACRES brownfield properties (lazy-loaded).
- [dod-fuds.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/dod-fuds.json): ~8,800 DOD Formerly Used Defense Sites.
- [dod-brac.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/dod-brac.json): 27 DOD BRAC base-closure sites.
- [infra-proximity.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/infra-proximity.json): per-site distances (miles) to transmission lines (+kV), substations (+kV), power plants (+MW & fuel), gas pipelines, rail, and highways, plus the FEMA flood-zone code and Special-Flood-Hazard-Area flag. Joined onto every program by `id`.
- [opportunity-zone.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/opportunity-zone.json): Treasury Qualified Opportunity Zone containment (tract GEOID + rural flag).
- [ira-energy-community.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/ira-energy-community.json): IRA (Inflation Reduction Act) energy-community designation per site — `in_energy_community` (bool), `energy_community_type` (`coal_closure` | `fossil_fuel_employment`), `energy_community_detail` (reason). Clean-energy projects on an energy community earn a +10 percentage-point ITC/PTC bonus under IRA §45/48. ~31.6% of sites qualify. Source: DOE NETL 2024 coal-closure tract + fossil-fuel-employment statistical-area layers (point-in-polygon).
- [iso-rto.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/iso-rto.json): ISO/RTO market (PJM, MISO, ERCOT, CAISO, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE, or non-RTO).
- [climate-zone.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/climate-zone.json): IECC/ASHRAE county climate zone.
- [fema-nri.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/fema-nri.json): FEMA National Risk Index per site (county-level) — `nri_risk_score` (0-100 composite), `nri_risk_rating`, and per-hazard ratings for the three DC-relevant hazards: `nri_wildfire_rating`, `nri_drought_rating`, `nri_heatwave_rating`. Wildfire/drought at Relatively-High or Very-High apply a climate penalty (−5 / −10) to both siting scores. 35,783 / 46,760 sites matched (CONUS counties). Source: FEMA NRI county FeatureServer (point-in-polygon).
- [epa-redev.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/epa-redev.json): EPA RE-Powering infrastructure-proximity flags + the data-center-reuse-candidate boolean (Superfund-only enrichment).
- [epa-echo.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/epa-echo.json): EPA ECHO enforcement & compliance summary (Superfund-only).
- [eia-retired-plants.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/eia-retired-plants.json): distance to the nearest large (≥100 MW) retired dispatchable power plant from EIA-860M (7,620 sites within 5 mi). Fields: `retired_plant_mi`, `retired_plant_mw`, `retired_plant_fuel`, `retired_plant_year`, `retired_plant_name`. Sites within 1 mi trigger the "Ret. Plant" badge and grid-inheritance scoring credit (the Conesville/Widows Creek pattern: inherited transmission + stranded interconnect agreement).
- [reference-campuses.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/reference-campuses.json): curated list of 10 confirmed hyperscale and colocation data center projects on brownfield / former industrial land (Google/Widows Creek coal plant AL, Aligned/Conesville coal plant OH, Homer City PA gas+DC campus, AWS/Susquehanna nuclear PA, Keystone Fairless Works steel mill PA, Project Marvel AL, Meta/Forest City textile mill NC, QTS/Qimonda fab VA, Cheswick coal plant PA, Microsoft/Foxconn site WI). Rendered as gold ★ overlay markers on the map; static JSON refreshed annually.
- [retired-industrial.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/retired-industrial.json): overlay of ~660 large RETIRED industrial sites nationwide that ceased EPA GHGRP reporting — ~530 manufacturing (NAICS 31–33: smelters, steel/paper mills, cement, glass, chemical plants, refineries, auto-assembly) + ~125 mining (NAICS 212, mostly coal mines/prep plants). Candidate data-center sites because a closed smelter/mill/refinery/mine may leave reusable grid infrastructure. Fields: `id`, `name`, `lat`, `lon`, `state`, `sector`, `category` (Manufacturing|Mining), `naics`, `last_report_year`, `reporting_status`, `parent_company`. Some sites also carry `tracked_site_id`/`tracked_site_name`/`tracked_site_mi`/`tracked_site_program` for the nearest tracked-program point within 1 mi (214/658); this is proximity context only, not parcel identity or availability evidence. Each marker popup cites the facility's EPA Envirofacts GHG record (`enviro.epa.gov/envirofacts/ghg/facility-detail/<id>`). Rendered as rust ◆ overlay markers. Generated by `scripts/build_retired_industrial.py` (spatially indexed proximity join; `--join-only` recomputes it); refresh after each annual GHGRP release.
- [planned-retirements.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/planned-retirements.json): overlay of ~90 OPERATING power plants ≥100 MW (75+ GW total) with ANNOUNCED retirement dates from the EIA-860M "Operating" sheet — a dated, forward-looking hand-off of a large grid interconnection (the Homer City pattern: replacement-generation/co-location deals are struck before shutdown). Fields: `id`, `name`, `lat`, `lon`, `state`, `county`, `mw`, `units_retiring`, `fuel` (coal|gas|oil|nuclear), `first_retirement_year`, `last_retirement_year`, `balancing_authority`, `operator`. Rendered as teal ⬢ overlay markers. Generated by `scripts/build_planned_retirements.py`; refresh alongside EIA-860M releases.
- [coord-quality.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/coord-quality.json): coordinate-confidence flags for the 3,991 sites whose location is demonstrably less trustworthy than the marker implies. Fields: `coord_flags` (any of `state_mismatch`, `outside_us`, `placeholder`, `shared_point`, `low_precision`), plus `coord_actual_state` / `coord_state_gap_mi` / `coord_shared_count` as evidence. **Absence means no known problem** — the other ~42.8k sites are omitted. Notably: 118 sites sit >1 mi outside the polygon of their own `state` field (13 of them >25 mi, 2 outside the US), and 3,728 share an exact coordinate with >=2 others, the signature of a geocoder falling back to a city centroid. The connector NEVER edits a coordinate — it labels one. Generated offline by `connectors/coord_quality.py` from the shipped `us-states.json` polygons; surfaced as a note under the detail panel's Coordinates row.
- [planned-retirements-proximity.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/planned-retirements-proximity.json): the per-site distance join of the planned-retirements overlay onto all 46,760 sites (614 within 5 mi). Fields: `planned_retirement_mi`, `planned_retirement_mw`, `planned_retirement_fuel`, `planned_retirement_year`, `planned_retirement_name`. Feeds the generation lens's `grid_reuse` score via a date-proximity multiplier (a plant retiring ≤3 yr out is as actionable as a recently-retired one) and the detail-panel "Retiring plant" row. Generated by `connectors/planned_retirements.py` (slug `planned-retirements-proximity`); re-run after regenerating the overlay.
- [ap1000-sites.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/ap1000-sites.json): curated AP1000 nuclear-reactor siting overlay — 14 named US military installations screened for hosting a Westinghouse AP1000 (1,117 MWe). Transmission/substation/gas/rail/highway are joined from infra-proximity.json; developable acreage, cooling water, fiber, and construction-workforce availability are analyst-researched, each with a per-field source URL. Source-program split: 9 sites are on the US Army "Janus" microreactor shortlist (Nov 2025), 5 are from the US Air Force AI-data-center Request for Lease (solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0002). A separate overlay (not part of the ~46,800-site brownfield corpus); rendered in the dashboard's Nuclear Siting tab (reactor-class selector: AP1000 / APR1400 large PWRs, AP300-class SMR, Janus-class microreactor), not on the map. Each site also carries a water-RIGHTS assessment (`water_rights_regime`, `water_rights_class` obtainable|contested|fully_appropriated, cited note) and, where documented, a drought low flow (`water_low_flow_cfs`). Generated by `scripts/build_ap1000_sites.py` (curated by hand; refreshed manually). Per-site water claims are validated with USGS streamgages + the Vogtle 3&4 environmental record in `ap1000-water-validation.md`.
- [ports.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/ports.json): live-fetched overlay of BTS/USACE Principal Ports (top 150 US ports by tonnage; 108 kept after filtering to `port_type` Coastal or Great Lakes, Internal river ports excluded) from the public `NTAD_Hazard_Exposure_Principal_Ports` FeatureServer. Fields: `name`, `port_type`, `lat`, `lon` (polygon bounding-box center), `hurricane_freq` (FEMA-NRI annual hurricane-strike frequency at the port). Rendered as ⚓ overlay markers. Generated by `scripts/build_ports_overlay.py`. Not part of the ~46,800-site corpus.
- [shipyards.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/shipyards.json): curated overlay of 16 major US heavy-shipbuilding/fabrication yards (no public GIS layer of US shipyards exists). Fields: `id`, `name`, `operator`, `city`, `state`, `lat`, `lon`, `capability` (`heavy_module` offshore platform/topsides fabrication | `large_hull` new construction | `naval_repair` drydock/overhaul only), `note`, `source_url`, `verified_at`. Rendered as ⚒ overlay markers. Generated by `scripts/build_shipyards.py`.
- [port-proximity.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/port-proximity.json): the per-site distance join of both overlays above onto all 46,759 sites. Tombstone convention: every site emits `{id, program}` even with nothing in range — `port_mi`/`shipyard_mi` absent means "checked, nothing within 75/150 mi" not "not yet checked". Fields when present: `port_mi`, `port_name`, `port_type`, `port_hurricane_freq`, `shipyard_mi`, `shipyard_name`, `shipyard_capability`. Feeds the two Maritime Siting lenses in `maritime-score.js` and the detail-panel "Nearest port"/"Nearest shipyard" rows. Generated by `connectors/port_proximity.py` (slug `port-proximity`).
- [streamgages.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/streamgages.json): live-fetched overlay of ACTIVE USGS streamflow gages carrying a published mean annual discharge, from the NWIS RDB web services. Fields: `gage_id`, `name`, `state`, `lat`, `lon`, `mean_flow_cfs`, `record_years`, `drainage_sqmi`. `mean_flow_cfs` is the mean of the gage's ANNUAL mean discharges over its period of record — a long-run average, NOT a permittable low-flow (7Q10) statistic, so it screens a candidate and never clears one. Generated by `scripts/build_streamgages_overlay.py`. Not part of the corpus.
- [water-proximity.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/water-proximity.json): the per-site join of the gage overlay onto all 46,759 sites — the project's first quantitative water signal (every earlier infrastructure layer moves electrons, freight or fuel). Tombstone convention. Fields when present: `water_gage_mi`, `water_flow_cfs`, `water_gage_name`, `water_gage_id`. `water_gage_mi` is distance to a GAGE, not to water; gages sit tens of miles apart on a large river. Generated by `connectors/water_proximity.py` (slug `water-proximity`).
- [nickel-anchors.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/nickel-anchors.json): curated catalog of the US nickel supply chain — feedstock mines and mills, recycled-feed projects, planned refineries, the one former US nickel refinery (Port Nickel, Braithwaite LA, 1958–2000), battery and stainless offtake, and bulk sulfuric-acid sources. Every row carries `source_url` + `verified_at`. `coord_precision` is `site` (a source located the facility) or `locality` (the Census Gazetteer internal point for a named place, good to a few miles) and must not be rendered as a facility coordinate. No authoritative live GIS layer of US mineral processing plants exists — the USGS dataset is a 2003 layer package. Rendered as ◈ overlay markers. Generated by `scripts/build_nickel_anchors.py`.
- [nickel-anchor-proximity.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/nickel-anchor-proximity.json): the per-site join of the anchor catalog. Tombstone convention, continental 1,000-mile range. Fields when present: `nickel_anchor_mi`, `nickel_anchor_name`, `nickel_anchor_kind`, `nickel_feedstock_mi`, `nickel_demand_mi`, `nickel_acid_mi`. Generated by `connectors/nickel_anchor_proximity.py`.
- [nuclear-civilian-sites.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/nuclear-civilian-sites.json): curated overlay of existing and planned CIVILIAN nuclear sites, tiered by Idaho National Laboratory's Aug-2024 study *Opportunities for AP1000 Deployment at Existing and Planned Nuclear Sites* (INL/MIS-24-80216) and extended with announced restarts and post-study entrants. Fields: `id`, `name`, `state`, `county`, `city`, `lat`, `lon`, `status`, `inl_category` (`dark_green` AP1000-ready | `light_green` AP1000-feasible | `blue` restart/SMR | `post_study` new entrant | `yellow` | `red`), `reactor_type`, `units_planned`, `mwe_per_unit`, `col_status`, `owner_operator`, `market`, `iso_rto`, `notes`, `nrc_url`. The four promising tiers render as ⚛ overlay markers on the map and as a table in the dashboard's Nuclear Siting tab; the yellow/red tiers are data-only. Not part of the ~46,800-site brownfield corpus (no SiteRecord join).
- [nuclear-brownfield-proximity.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/nuclear-brownfield-proximity.json): per-nuclear-site list of tracked EPA Superfund sites within `radius_mi` (50 mi) of each site in nuclear-civilian-sites.json — `{nuclear_site_id, nuclear_site_name, state, lat, lon, inl_category, nearby_brownfields: [{id, name, city, state, lat, lon, program, npl_status, acreage, distance_mi}]}`. Surfaced in each ⚛ marker popup as the top-3 nearest, deep-linked by `?site=<id>`.
- [microreactor-fleet.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/microreactor-fleet.json): curated reference layer for the microreactor market — 12 vendor designs (11 in the 1–20 MWe band plus Oklo's Aurora as a labelled adjacency), 32 named commitments, and an 8-sector / 55-class demand ladder. Vendor fields: `id`, `name`, `design`, `mwe_low`/`mwe_high`/`mwt`, `coolant`, `fuel`, `refuel_years`, `footprint_acres`, `transport`, `band`, `band_basis`, `ticker`, `funding_usd`, `commercial`, `anpi_site`, `sources[]`, `gaps[]`. Commitment fields: `id`, `track` (`us-gov`|`us-commercial`|`intl`), `vendor_id`, `owner`, `sector`, `location`, `state`, `lat`/`lon`, `power_label`, `mwe`, `timeline`, `instrument`, `status`, `band`, `microreactor`, `sources[]`, `gaps[]`. `band` is one of six evidence bands carried verbatim from the Deployment Core project (operational | construction | doe-authorized | review | contracted | framework) — capacity is summed ONLY within a band, never across them, so `committed_mwe_by_band` is a mapping and there is deliberately no total. The nine Army Janus installations take their coordinates from ap1000-sites.json rather than carrying their own. 24 rows carry coordinates and render as purple ⬣ overlay markers. Not part of the ~46,800-site corpus (no SiteRecord join). Generated by `scripts/build_microreactor_fleet.py`.
- [coal-conversions.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/coal-conversions.json): curated overlay of prominent US coal plants (operating | planned_retirement | retired | converted_gas, ≥100 MW) screened for nuclear-SMR / AI-data-center conversion — switchyard kV, rail loop, water intake, ISO/RTO, a MODELED stranded-asset value (screening estimate, formula in `scripts/build_coal_conversions.py`), and derived POI-reuse eligibility (`queue_transfer_eligible`, false for operating plants). Every row carries `source_url` + `verified_at` (quarterly re-audit — retirement dates move under DOE §202(c) orders and data-center-driven life extensions). Rendered as ⬢ markers and the Coal Reinvestment tab.
- [coal-conversions-proximity.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/coal-conversions-proximity.json): per-site join of the coal catalog onto the corpus (nearest asset ≤10 mi): `coal_conversion_{plant_name,plant_mi,mw,switchyard_kv,rail,water,stranded_val_usd,queue_fasttrack}`. Feeds the detail-panel "Coal reinvestment" row.
- [federal-clean-energy.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/federal-clean-energy.json): curated overlay of DOE "Cleanup to Clean Energy" / AI-data-centers-on-federal-land / OCED CEML mine-lands sites (SRS, INL, Hanford, WIPP, NNSS, Paducah — Brookfield/NextEra award, Portsmouth, Oak Ridge ETTP, Mineral Basin solar, Lewis Ridge pumped storage) with program stage, partners, acreage, and per-row `solicitation_url` + `verified_at`. Rendered as 🏛 markers.
- [hanford-e2e.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/hanford-e2e.json): the Hanford NEPA dossier (the "DOE Sites" tab's default site) — 9 named land units of the 580-sq-mi DOE site, each with curated ground truth (`source_url` + `verified_at` per row), a ten-source PNNL nepa-mcp environmental screen (USFWS IPaC, NOAA West Coast critical habitat, salmon EFH, tribal geography, NRHP, PAD-US, USACE district, FEMA NFHL, GBIF, EPA NEPAssist), joins from this dashboard's own infra enrichments, nearby tracked records, opportunity fits (`anchored`/`strong`/`conditional`/`precluded`), a `facility_fit` comparison per parcel across four facility types (data center, large reactor LWR/PWR, SMR, microreactor — each cell carrying a `constraint` naming its binding factor plus optional per-cell `sources`), and a seven-category `infrastructure` list (power_td, natural_gas, water, rail, road, fiber, workforce), every row carrying `source_url` + `verified_at`. The payload's `narrative_note` discloses that the prose is AI-drafted from those sources and checked against them. Per-parcel 14-layer GeoJSON map packages (incl. EPA EIS boundaries) live under `data/hanford-nepa/`. This is screening evidence, not an agency determination; a source recorded as unavailable is different from a result of zero. Generated by `scripts/build_hanford_e2e.py`.
- [srs-e2e.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/srs-e2e.json), [portsmouth-e2e.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/portsmouth-e2e.json), [paducah-e2e.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/paducah-e2e.json), [wipp-e2e.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/wipp-e2e.json): sibling DOE-site dossiers (Savannah River SC, Portsmouth OH, Paducah KY, WIPP NM — the "DOE Sites" tab's site switcher), same payload shape as `hanford-e2e.json` but with an eight-source nepa-mcp screen (the two Pacific-marine tools — NOAA West Coast critical habitat and salmon EFH — are geographically inapplicable and deliberately absent from `sources`). 17 land units total covering the 2025-2026 federal AI-data-center awards (Portsmouth's PORTS Technology Campus under construction, Paducah's Brookfield/NextEra award, SRS's Amentum lease negotiation), the operating missions (Centrus HALEU, DUF6, the WIPP repository), transferred/reuse parcels (SODI/Trillium/Oklo, General Matter), and the honestly-precluded land. Per-parcel GeoJSON map packages live under `data/<site>-nepa/`. Generated by `scripts/build_doe_sites_e2e.py`.
- [coal-nepa.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/coal-nepa.json): per-plant NEPA permitting screens for the 18-plant coal reinvestment catalog (seven nepa-mcp sources each: IPaC, tribal, NRHP, PAD-US point, USACE district, NFHL flood zones, NEPAssist), keyed by `plant_name`. Rendered as the Coal drawer's "Permitting screen" chips. Counts mean buffer-intersections, not the plant parcel; riverine plants near mapped flood zones are expected context, not a disqualifier. Generated by `scripts/build_coal_nepa.py`.
- [epa-superfund-docs.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/epa-superfund-docs.json): curated federal documents per Superfund site (RODs, Five-Year Reviews, fact sheets).
- [ai-summary.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/ai-summary.json): one-paragraph plain-English site summaries synthesized from the structured fields.
- [coal-plants.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/coal-plants.json): every US coal plant with >=100 MW of coal retired or scheduled to retire, from EIA-860M (244 plants), with nearest HIFLD line, other operating MW at the plant, and curated project notes where they match.
- [population-centers.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/population-centers.json): 1,606 Census places of 25,000+ (Vintage 2024) with coordinates, for the 10 CFR 100.3 population-center check.
- [acreage-flags.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/acreage-flags.json): reported acreages that describe a county, a region, a river or a groundwater plume rather than a parcel; screens treat them as unknown.
- [infra-proximity-core.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/brownfield-opportunities/data/infra-proximity-core.json): distance and voltage fields of infra-proximity.json only (loaded at startup).

## Methods & schema

- [screens.js](https://github.com/pranava0x0/brownfield-opportunities/blob/main/docs/screens.js): every ranking. `SiteScreens.evaluate(site, key)` returns pass/fail/unknown per check; `SiteScreens.rank(sites, key)` orders by checks met, then unknowns, then the screen's tie-breaker. Each check carries its rule, threshold source URL, and an R (agency threshold: EPA RE-Powering, FEMA, NRC, Army, EIA) or P (our threshold) tag.
- [evidence-categories.js](https://github.com/pranava0x0/brownfield-opportunities/blob/main/docs/evidence-categories.js): per-site findings and confidence for grid, water, land, logistics and hazards, shown under the checks in the site panel.
- [provenance.js](https://github.com/pranava0x0/brownfield-opportunities/blob/main/docs/provenance.js): field-level registry mapping each value to its publisher, dataset and a per-site verification link.
- [schema.py](https://github.com/pranava0x0/brownfield-opportunities/blob/main/schema.py): the `SiteRecord` Pydantic schema. Each record sets `id` (cross-source unique) and `program` (`superfund` | `brownfield` | `fuds` | `brac`).

## Notes

- Distances are in miles; values over 100 mi are dropped as out-of-CONUS. A distance of `0.0` means "adjacent" (borders the boundary), not missing.
- Acreage is unavailable for all ACRES brownfields and ~66% of FUDS sites (source-side gaps, not omissions) — those fall to the bottom of acreage sorts and render "—".
- Flood-zone coverage is partial; a missing `in_sfha` is unknown, not "no risk".
- Data refreshes on a cron via GitHub Actions; the dashboard shows the refresh date next to the site title (`#topbar-refresh`) — the single readout on the page as of 2026-08-24 (it used to be duplicated in the hero, footer, and subtitle tagline).
